correctness.rationale: For the repaired claim, length-p increasing paths only use first-superdiagonal steps or one second-superdiagonal step. Both first-superdiagonal products must vanish. Any two nonadjacent zero positions force the remaining entry to vanish. A single zero must be interior; factoring the top entry leaves precisely the indicated determinant. Two adjacent zeros leave a nonzero coefficient times b_i, and either interior zero index gives the corresponding Q_k when b_i=0. The converse follows by the same factorization without dividing by any entries. Each determinant is irreducible over any extension (e.g. primitive linear in one variable with coprime coefficients), and its degree-one vanishing ideal is spanned by a_k. This distinguishes the equidimensional Q_k from each other and the P_ij, proves maximality, and gives the linear and nonlinear counts. The smaller-size assertions follow directly from path length. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/review_evidence/reproduce.py 2` compared powers applied to all basis vectors with component membership on all 59,049 full matrices for p=q=3, giving 22,113 points; the p=q=2 boundary check gives 28 of 64. The old point formula is correct as well, but the repaired document explains why it is prior-derived.
residual_risks: Bounded numerical checks are not a proof for every field. The result concerns the reduced locus, not reducedness or scheme-theoretic primary decomposition of the power ideal.

evidence: Only (n) and (n−1,1) with n=p+2 are excluded. For their counts A_n and B_n, Proposition 3.1 yields A_n=q^(n−2)(q−1)A_(n−1) and B_n=q^(n−2)((q−1)B_(n−1)+A_(n−1)) for n≥4. A_3=q(q−1)² and the worked example gives B_3=(q−1)(2q+1).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus B_n/A_n=((n−1)q+1)/(q(q−1)), and A_n+B_n=q^((n−1)(n−2)/2−1)(q−1)^(n−2)(q²+(n−2)q+1). Its subtraction gives the frozen polynomial verbatim. No comparable implication for the explicit geometric P/Q stratification was found.

value.rationale: The repaired claim identifies the exact first nonlinear geometry in a natural restricted-nullcone family. The numerical tableau count alone does not distinguish linear coordinate components from determinantal cones or locate them in the original matrix coordinates; the result supplies those components and their defining constraints uniformly. Value is not assigned to the prior-derived point count or to the numerical component count alone.
